- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly or allow downward drift.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–10 day average if deviation > 3σ.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon; apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 1–2% per day from forecast if sentiment is flat or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast trajectory.
